sourceEvidence.label: nimrod CACIS owner brief and constitutional architecture collection

assessment.summary: One structural opportunity can add dynamic world modeling and immune organisms while preserving nimrod's existing constitutional authority and verification boundaries.

nonNegotiables: Doctrine v0.1 remains governing and unchanged.
The Sovereign Governor and immune organisms cannot authorize execution.
Operational offense remains behind existing Crucible gates.
Evolution cannot change authority, trust, constitution, or safety ceilings.
assumptions: No measured CACIS runtime latency, memory, scale, or deployment budget was supplied.
The first implementation remains unprivileged, deterministic, and replay-only.

opportunities.title: Constitutional immune plane
opportunities.summary: Separate mutable world modeling, temporary organisms, metacognition, and genome learning from immutable authority and effect execution.
opportunities.diagnosis: Adding every CACIS responsibility directly to the current fixed swarm would concentrate truth formation, scheduling, memory, and learning in one long-lived ownership boundary.

evidence.claim: The owner brief requests a living world model, temporary organisms, metacognition, genome learning, and recursive improvement while preserving authority.
Doctrine separates analysis, authorization, execution, verification, evidence, and human authority.
The current architecture already has distinct kernel, executor, verifier, Witness, Foundry, and display ownership.
A fixed swarm enlarged to own mutable world state, lifecycle, and memory would create correlated integrity and availability risk even if its formal maximum outcome remained a proposal.

desiredInvariants: Immutable observations remain distinct from versioned derived state.
Only the existing Constitutional Kernel may authorize deterministic policy and it cannot execute.
The Governor schedules but cannot authorize; organisms propose but cannot execute.
Consequential claims and recovery are independently verified.
Genome output remains inert candidate data under partitioned evaluation.
Public hosts and unknown ownership are never offensive targets.

options.title: Extend the current swarm
options.summary: Add permanent roles and an in-process shared world model to the current proposal swarm.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: It prototypes requested cognition but does not structurally isolate truth, lifecycle, and learning.
Local checks can retain the proposal ceiling while future ownership drift remains possible.

tradeoffs.assessment: More typed challenge improves proposal quality, but mutable state is concentrated.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Threat-model internal role bypass and replay poisoned shared state.

tradeoffs.assessment: Shared-memory calls likely avoid transport overhead for small replay workloads.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure fixed-corpus p50 and p95 replay latency against Option 2.

tradeoffs.assessment: One runtime likely duplicates less infrastructure, though retained state is unbounded until designed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare peak RSS and retained bytes per event.

tradeoffs.assessment: A larger shared crash and corruption domain couples more cognitive functions.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject crashes and corrupt shared generations during replay.

tradeoffs.assessment: It introduces no new deployable service.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise upgrade, rollback, and state-rebuild procedures.

tradeoffs.assessment: Existing swarm and board contracts can be extended locally.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run existing swarm and board validators unchanged.

residualRisks: Truth, lifecycle, memory, and scheduling remain correlated.
Verifier independence can erode inside one ownership domain.

acceptanceCriteria: No action edge and deterministic replay.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Remove the new roles and shared state consumers.

options.title: Federated constitutional immune plane
options.summary: Add explicit world-model, organism, hypothesis, settlement, and genome planes around existing immutable controls.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: It maps requested capabilities to bounded outcomes and staged contracts.
It preserves the existing kernel, independent verification, and authority ceilings.
It keeps all offensive effects behind existing Crucible gates.
It keeps genome output candidate-only under partitioned evaluation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Every mutable plane has an explicit non-executing maximum outcome and causal evidence boundary.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Reject authority widening, self-verification, target contact, and sealed-evaluator leakage.

tradeoffs.assessment: Versioned generations and typed serialization add work to replay and investigation paths.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure p50/p95 generation and settlement latency on fixed corpora.

tradeoffs.assessment: Immutable observations, generations, queues, and indexes retain additional bounded state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak RSS and retained bytes per event under explicit retention windows.

tradeoffs.assessment: Organisms are disposable and derived state is rebuildable, though the world model becomes critical.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Crash and rebuild at every observation-to-generation boundary.

tradeoffs.assessment: Generation health, organism lifecycle, backlog, and verifier capacity require new observability.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rehearse degraded state, drain, rollback, and incident diagnostics.

tradeoffs.assessment: Wave-by-wave dual reads preserve current consumers but require versioned migrations.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare old projections and new derived generations before cutover.

residualRisks: The world-model store becomes a critical integrity and availability dependency.
Correlated cells can still share poisoned inputs.

workPackages: Complete W0 through W7 in order.
acceptanceCriteria: Each plane enforces its maximum outcome and every wave exits on evidence.
migrationNotes: Begin offline and dual-read; no action edge through W2.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable CACIS scheduling and consumers, drain the current generation, and return to existing projections.

options.title: Service-per-cell immune mesh
options.summary: Deploy world model, Governor, cells, challengers, settlement, genome, and Observatory as independently identified services.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: It implements the full organism vision with strong deployable isolation options.
Distinct identities can strengthen separation, but the event mesh and service identity become new trusted controls.

tradeoffs.assessment: Distinct service identities can narrow blast radius while adding broker, network, and identity attack surface.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compromise one cell identity and prove cross-plane denial.

tradeoffs.assessment: Network hops, copies, and serialization enter the critical path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure end-to-end event-to-settlement latency under target load.

tradeoffs.assessment: Per-service runtimes, buffers, caches, and sidecars duplicate resident state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure aggregate resident memory at minimum and peak topology.

tradeoffs.assessment: Local fault isolation improves while distributed partial failures, retries, and ordering can reduce system reliability.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run broker loss, partition, duplicate, reorder, retry-storm, and clock-skew campaigns.

tradeoffs.assessment: Deployment, identity, key rotation, tracing, queue health, and incident response expand substantially.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rehearse deploy, rotate, rollback, and compromise containment with an operations owner.

tradeoffs.assessment: Dual publishing, compatibility windows, service identity, and queue draining are required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prove mixed-version compatibility and rollback without stale acceptance.

residualRisks: The event mesh becomes a critical trust and availability boundary.
Separate processes can still share correlated operators, images, keys, and poisoned inputs.

affectedComponents: future deployment and service identity plane
workPackages: Define measured decomposition triggers before implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: Measured scale or isolation need justifies distributed cost.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Drain a complete generation and restore federated local routing.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the federated constitutional immune plane now; select the service mesh only when measured scale, tenant isolation, fault containment, or ownership requires deployable separation.

openQuestions: What W1 event volume, retention, latency, recovery, and device-resource budgets should govern storage choices?
Which memory strata may contain customer telemetry, and under what retention and deletion policy?
Who owns private and external evaluator custody?
